verdict.rationale: SharePoint documents a public REST service, usable from any technology that can make REST web requests, with full CRUD (create, read, update, delete), update and recycle operations and OData $batch support. It is also exposed through Microsoft Graph with read-write access to lists, listItems, driveItems and tenant settings, which gives an AI-native user a documented programmatic surface. One community report notes OAuth permissions can't be scoped to particular sites, but that limits access granularity rather than contradicting the API. Missing for 10: a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (the probe paths returned 404), independent hands-on corroboration of API reliability, and finer-grained per-site OAuth scoping.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Now, developers can interact remotely with SharePoint data by using any technology that supports REST web requests.
Perform basic CRUD operations on folders and files with the SharePoint REST interface.
The SharePoint Online (and on-premises SharePoint 2016 or later) REST service supports combining multiple requests into a single call to the service by using the OData `$batch` query option.
